summary.headline: H1 FY27 standalone total income rose about 182% to INR52.37 crore, with PAT up about 395% to INR6.85 crore, as a carried-over order book was executed.
summary.overview: Robokidz Eduventures reported H1 FY27 (half year to 30 Sep 2026), its first earnings call after listing on the BSE SME platform on 28 Sep 2026 (subscribed 834 times). Standalone total income rose to INR52.37 crore from INR18.55 crore, EBITDA to INR11.53 crore and PAT to INR6.85 crore. Consolidated revenue from operations was INR60.67 crore, EBITDA INR13.93 crore (about 22.9% margin) and PAT INR7.93 crore. Management attributed the jump to execution of a large order carried over from FY26 plus new institutional orders, and said H2 will be much smaller in relative terms. Working capital remained high at about INR73 crore, which management tied to government payment cycles, with collections expected in H2 and December-January.

financial_highlights.change: up approx 182% from INR18.55 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR7.93 crore after tax of INR3.02 crore
approx INR73 crore at H1 end
financial_highlights.change: FY26 year-end approx INR62 crore; receivables approx INR72 crore at FY26 year-end

segments.name: Lab setup (institutional / government)
segments.commentary: Management said about 75% of revenue comes from lab setups, with EBITDA margin of about 18-20%. Government customers are about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: Subscription and other education services
segments.commentary: About 25% of revenue per management, with EBITDA margin of about 28-30%. Service income was about 12.8% of H1 revenue, and 60% of it comes from existing customers. Last year the mix was 95% lab setup and 5% services.

segments.name: YEA centres (Robokidz Retails Pvt Ltd, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Management said YEA contributes about 25% of top line; EBITDA about 28-30% and PAT about 17-18%. Four stores are operating, three new Pune centres are due by December 2026, and 5-10 more are in pipeline, mainly in western India. Management said YEA is a separate business from subscriptions.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth target of 30-35% a year.
FY27 revenue split between H1 and H2 expected around 35:65, versus 20:80 in FY26.
Confirmed H2 order book of about INR75 crore, expected to be executed by 31 March 2027 (INR10 crore executed so far). Management expects a further INR25-30 crore of orders, unconfirmed.
Around 12-15 company-owned YEA stores planned by March 2027 (management comment).
Big government tenders expected in December-January.
Management said margins can be maintained as the business grows and that operating leverage is expected.
capex_capacity: Three new YEA centres in Pune (Hadapsar, Amanora Park Town, Kharadi, Viman Nagar), with start expected by December 2026.
Labs set up last year (FY26 capex) are now starting service models, which management said is driving the shift to subscriptions.
IPO proceeds are being used as stated in the prospectus, mainly working capital and prepayment.
Management said H1 covered around 1,100 schools across three states.
demand_pricing: Order book: management cited INR75 crore of confirmed orders for execution by March 2027. Earlier, in answer to a separate question, it cited an H1 order book of INR56 crore, of which INR52 crore was executed.
Demand driver: the CBSE composite skill lab requirement, with schools expected to comply by August 2027 (extension possible). Government budgets are said to be allocated for the next five years.

Procurement: government tenders are won through channel partners in each state and are subject to technical qualification (turnover, experience) before financial bids open. Management said L1 pricing decides the award.
Retention: management said 80% of private-school clients are retained, including some that have been customers for 14-15 years. Clients are not named because of NDAs.
Management declined to give tender win rates, bid counts, pricing or quote-to-order ratios.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital and receivables so high (about INR73 crore vs H1 revenue of about INR60 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Government customers pay on milestones and budget cycles. H1 collections are expected in H2, and H2 collections in the next H1. Management said the normal working capital cycle is 120-130 days. Government is the main slow payer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need equity or debt funding in FY28 (an analyst estimated INR15-18 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board will decide and it will disclose to the exchange. It said the company 'might need' external funds, but could not say how much.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from the YEA franchise model and its share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give YEA revenue for the call. It said YEA would contribute about 20-25% of revenue, and that three centres are signed with more being scouted.

qa_highlights.question: How much order book is there, and how much can be executed by March?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed order book is INR75 crore, expected to be executed by 31 March 2027, with INR10 crore executed so far. Another INR25-30 crore is expected but not confirmed. Management declined to share quote conversion ratios or pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR75 crore order book include service income, and how much of service income comes from existing customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR75 crore is new lab orders only, and service income sits on top. Around 60% of service income is from existing customers and 40% from new ones.

qa_highlights.question: When will bigger tenders come, and is private school business part of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bigger tenders are expected in December-January. Private school business is part of the subscription model in Robokidz Retail, not the tender book.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: about INR73 crore at H1 with government collections slow. Management expects H2 collections, and analysts flagged possible negative operating cash flow.
Possible FY28 external funding need (analyst estimate INR15-18 crore); board decision still pending.
Order book is mostly tender-driven and channel-partner dependent. Management did not give win rates, pricing or repeat-tender data.
Growth in H2 is expected to be much slower than H1 (35:65 split). Growth in H1 was partly due to a one-off carry-over order.
Related-party question: Robokidz Retail's FY26 sales of INR41.6 crore were explained as sourcing from other suppliers for customised private-school BOQs; the answer was not fully clear.
YEA revenue is not disclosed; a franchise pipeline of 5-10 centres is unverified.
Watch: Pune YEA centres going live by December 2026, December-January tender awards, and H2 collections.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 numbers and the growth outlook, but evasive on specifics. Management declined to disclose YEA revenue, tender win rates, pricing, quote ratios and client names (citing NDAs). It also gave unclear answers on funding needs and on the Robokidz Retail supply question.

growth.why: Management targets 30-35% annual revenue growth (midpoint 32.5%) backed by a confirmed H2 order book of INR75 crore to be executed by March 2027 and 12-15 owned YEA stores by March 2027, though the H1 jump is largely a carried-over order and H2 is guided to be much smaller, and the 30-35% multi-year target is not tied to specific orders beyond FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management cites a sustainable consolidated EBITDA margin of 22-23% against H1's 22.9%, and says operating leverage is expected, but H1 was lifted by a carried-over order and H2 is guided to be much smaller, so expansion above that band is not supported.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Three Pune YEA centres are due by December 2026 and management plans 12-15 company-owned YEA stores by March 2027, up from four operating today.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Confirmed H2 order book of INR75 crore to be executed by March 2027 (INR10 crore done so far), plus a further INR25-30 crore unconfirmed, against H1 revenue of INR60.67 crore, though H2 is expected to be much smaller relative to H1 (35:65 split).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said the board may need external equity or debt funding in FY28 (analyst estimate INR15-18 crore) with a board decision pending, and working capital is about INR73 crore; no utilisation figure was given so a plant capex is not indicated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on H1 and expects INR25-30 crore of unconfirmed orders plus December-January tenders, but guided no numeric upgrade and H2 is smaller.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 is guided to be much slower than H1, working capital is about INR73 crore with slow government collections, and the 30-35% growth target depends on tenders management would not quantify (win rates and pricing undisclosed).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management described service and subscription models (service income about 12.8% of H1 revenue) and YEA franchise expansion of 5-10 more centres in the pipeline, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Working capital release in H2 and Dec-Jan
rows.why: Working capital is about INR73 crore vs H1 revenue of INR60.67 crore, and management expects H1 collections in H2 and H2 collections in the next H1, but government payment cycles are slow and the 120-130 day cycle is unchanged.

rows.label: CBSE composite skill lab demand and December-January tenders
rows.why: Management expects big government tenders in December-January, with the CBSE skill lab compliance deadline of August 2027 and budgets allocated for five years, though win rates and pricing were not disclosed.
